turn_text: Good Wednesday morning, I'm Anna Palmer, and welcome to your Politico playbook flash briefing brought to you by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. We sat down with Senator Chuck Schumer on his first day as Minority Leader, and he revealed a brand new Democratic messaging campaign seeking to paint an apocalyptic picture of America when Republicans repeal Obamacare. Get ready to hear Democrats repeatedly riff on Donald Trump's campaign slogan that Republicans will make America sick again. Schumer also used the word Chaos several times to describe Republicans' repeal of Obamacare and how it would create madness across the country. The New York Democrat pledged that Democrats won't be helping Republicans figure out Obamacare alternatives. And we have some exclusive news today. Josh Bolton, George W. Bush's former White House Chief of Staff, will be the next president and CEO of the Business Roundtable replacing former Michigan Governor John Engler. Politico and Morning Consult are out this morning with a new poll that found 70% of voters want Trump to talk about healing the country in his inaugural address. And another interesting nugget in the poll, just 43% had heard not much or nothing about the UN's resolution condemning Israel for building in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. President Barack Obama is huddling with Senate Democrats while Vice President-elect Mike Pence will meet with both Senate and House Republicans to discuss health care. He's expected to take questions following the House Republican meeting. Subscribe to Playbook at political.com slash playbook.

explicit_propositions.text: Anna Palmer is presenting the POLITICO Playbook flash briefing.
The briefing is sponsored by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.
Senator Chuck Schumer was interviewed on his first day as Minority Leader.
Democrats are launching a new messaging campaign portraying Republican repeal of Obamacare as apocalyptic.
Schumer referenced Donald Trump’s campaign slogan 'Make America Sick Again' in opposition to Republican healthcare plans.
Schumer described Republican efforts to repeal Obamacare using the term 'chaos'.
Democrats will not assist Republicans in developing alternative healthcare proposals.
Josh Bolton, former White House Chief of Staff under George W. Bush, will become the next president and CEO of the Business Roundtable.
A joint poll by POLITICO and Morning Consult shows 70% of voters believe Trump should focus on healing the nation in his inaugural address.

assumptions.text: Political narratives shape public perception more than factual accuracy.
Media framing influences audience interpretation of political events.
Partisan alignment determines credibility and rhetorical strategy.
Public figures gain legitimacy through institutional affiliations (e.g., Senate leadership, presidential staff).
Audiences expect media to provide curated, narrative-driven summaries over raw event reporting.
Negative framing (e.g., apocalypse, chaos) enhances message impact in political communication.
Leadership transitions signal shifts in policy priorities and power dynamics.
Polling data serves as authoritative evidence to justify editorial positioning.
International issues receive less attention unless tied to domestic political relevance.
Subscribers value exclusivity and insider access in news consumption.
